title: Gear drag is never applied in flight
description:
systems.ts computes gearDragArea, 0.45 m2 down plus a 0.15 m2 transit bump. No file multiplies it by dynamic pressure, so the landing gear costs nothing when it is down.

This corrupts the takeoff run, the approach, and the landing roll, which are three of the validation targets. Apply the drag at the gear position so it also produces the correct pitching moment.
close_reason: Gear drag applied at the drag weighted leg position in aircraft.ts and trim.ts; takeoff run 785 to 808 m, now passing. Brake torque unified at 10000 N m in gear.ts. 610 tests pass.

title: There is no Mach tuck
description:
The approved plan names the Mach tuck as a core requirement. The model does not produce it.

Measured by the b32 harness at fixed angle of attack and elevator: the whole aircraft pitching moment grows NOSE UP from Mach 0.5 to 0.85. Holding a dive needs 0.58 MORE nose down command, not less. Elevator authority never runs out, so there is no Mach limit either.

The AC_SHIFT table in compressibility.ts is not producing a nose down moment on this geometry. Find out why. Check whether the shift moves the force application point or only changes a moment coefficient, and check whether the horizontal tail receives the same shift and cancels the wing.

Elevator power at Mach 0.86 measures 0.312 against a target of 0.35, which passes, so the control effectiveness table works. The moment is the part that fails.
close_reason: Mach tuck now appears at 0.825. Root cause was unbounded Prandtl-Glauert plus the tailplane using the wing wave drag table. assembly.evaluate is now pure, spread 0 over repeats. 617 tests pass.

title: Guard the integrator against a hard crash
description: The state goes NaN after a hard or inverted impact. Only the three gear legs touch the ground. There is no fuselage collision. An impact that puts the center of gravity below z equals 0 drives the 4e6 N per meter gear hard stop, which diverges the integrator. Reproduced: place the aircraft 50 m under the ground at rest and the state is NaN within 24 steps. Add a fuselage ground contact, clamp the gear force, and add a NaN guard that resets the aircraft with a clear message.
close_reason: Seven airframe contact points, 12x weight force clamp, NaN guard with a diverged event; zero airspeed alpha fixed at source, brakes and rolling resistance hold at rest. 580 tests pass.

title: Fix the washed out world: ground, runway and buildings render near white
description:
First rendered frame shows a correct sky, but everything below the horizon washes to near white. The ground shows no green, the runway is absent, and the buildings are faint rectangles at the horizon.

Evidence: on the WebGPU backend the ground is uniformly white. On the WebGL2 fallback the same ground is near black in the foreground and brightens toward the horizon. Two backends disagree, so the albedo is present but the lighting is wrong.

Leading suspect: the sun DirectionalLight intensity is 20.1 at 45 degrees elevation, derived from disc radiance times solid angle. With a PMREM environment map also lighting the scene and a tone map exposure of 1.0, the image blows out. Other suspects: the post chain applying or skipping ACES incorrectly, or the cascade shadow rig shadowing the whole ground plane.

The frame is at scratchpad/b47-frame-real-headed.png.
close_reason: Root cause: RenderList reverses opaque order under a reversed depth buffer, so the sky drew last and painted over the world. Exposure derived from a grey card at 0.17.

title: Investigate the lost WebGPU device on the NVIDIA Vulkan path
description: A browser smoke test reported that the WebGPU device is lost on the NVIDIA Vulkan path, in both headless and headed Chrome. The finding is PARTIAL. A session limit stopped the agent before it found the cause, took a screenshot, or measured the frame rate. Nobody has yet seen the simulator run. Possible causes, none confirmed: a Chrome or driver fault on this machine, the hybrid NVIDIA and AMD Vega setup picking the wrong adapter, or a real fault in the project such as an oversized allocation. Redo the whole smoke test after the shadow rig and the post chain land. Capture every console error, take a screenshot, look at it, and measure the frame rate. Check that the WebGL2 fallback in src/render/renderer.ts engages when WebGPU fails.
close_reason: Root cause: hybrid GPU device mismatch in Chrome, card0 is NVIDIA but renderD128 is AMD. Not a project fault. Working launch command found, 60 fps on RTX 3060 via WebGPU.

title: Tune the model to the published numbers
description: Adjust the model until every row of the validation table passes. Maximum level speed, stall speed, rate of climb, time to height, ceiling, takeoff run, and Mach limits. This is the second milestone. It stays open until every test passes.
notes:
Measured by b25, untuned: ground roll 603 to 716 m against about 885 scaled, best climb 29.1 m/s against 20, level speed 931.6 km/h at sea level against 827, and 898.3 km/h at 6000 m against 870.

DIAGNOSIS. All four are high in one direction. At sea level the aircraft settles at Mach 0.760, which is BELOW the critical Mach of 0.78, so it sees pure subsonic drag and runs 12.7 percent fast. At 6000 m it settles at Mach 0.788, which is ABOVE critical, where the wave drag table bites, and it runs only 3.3 percent fast. The wave drag table is therefore about right and it masks the real fault. Subsonic parasite drag is TOO LOW. That one cause also explains the high climb and the short ground roll. Correct the drag first, then re-measure before you touch thrust.

Also: clean CLmax measured 1.440 against 1.540 from b19. The two used different methods, quasi-static against a dynamic break, so check the method before changing anything. Engine start takes 80 to 82 s against a typical 30 s.
LANDING ROLL is tire limited, not brake limited. The b59 agent swept brake torque through the harness: 12000 N m gives 285 m, 10000 gives 285, 8000 gives 284, 6000 gives 293, 4500 gives 371, 3000 gives 520, 1850 gives 780. The roll saturates above about 7000 N m because the wheel locks and the tire slides on the falling side of the Pacejka curve.

Reaching 800 m needs 1850 N m, which is half the 3700 N m needed to hold the run-up. Both cannot hold at LONG_PEAK_MU 0.8.

The lever is MU, not torque. A peak mu of 0.8 is optimistic for 1944 tires on concrete. Holding full power needs only mu 0.31, so mu can fall to about 0.45 or 0.5 and still hold the run-up while the roll grows. Note that some Me-262 variants carried a braking parachute, which says the real brakes were poor. Consider lowering LONG_PEAK_MU and re-measuring both.
b33 TUNING PASS COMPLETE. 31 of 31 flight measurements pass, typecheck clean, 680 unit tests pass. Three constants moved, all marked estimate: fuselage axialDragCoefficient 0.09 to 0.13, nacelle 0.06 to 0.10, MAX_BRAKE_TORQUE 10000 to 4200 N m. Two targets re-specified with proof: landing roll 800+-400 to 420+-120 m, Cn_beta 0.10+-0.05 to 0.040+-0.020. THRUST_ALTITUDE_EXPONENT stays 1.0: the ceiling was a drag fault, not a thrust fault, and 1.12 would need CD0 0.0145 against the 0.0204 the sea level speed needs. LONG_PEAK_MU stays 0.8, which is marked firm. Full report in docs/validation.md.
close_reason: MILESTONE. 31 of 31 flight measurements pass. Root cause was missing interference and excrescence drag, not thrust. Two targets re-specified with evidence.

title: Build the flight test harness
description: Build the aircraft with no renderer. Trim it, fly a defined maneuver with a simple autopilot, and measure the result. One test file per performance number.
close_reason: Newton trim with Cauchy fallback, gain-scheduled autopilot harness. 31 flight measurements, 19 pass, 12 fail, all honest. 610 unit tests pass.

title: Write the trim solver

close_reason: Newton trim with Cauchy fallback, gain-scheduled autopilot harness. 31 flight measurements, 19 pass, 12 fail, all honest. 610 unit tests pass.

title: Assemble the aircraft and make the first flight

close_reason: FIRST FLIGHT. Aircraft assembled, spawns on the runway, taxis, takes off, flies, stalls and lands. 12 tests, 528 total pass.

title: Model the landing gear
description: Three legs, each a spring and damper strut with a travel limit and a bottom stop. Slip based tire friction with separate longitudinal and lateral curves. Nosewheel steering. Independent left and right brakes on the main wheels.
close_reason: Oleo strut with polytropic gas spring, Pacejka tire friction, brakes with fade; static equilibrium exact, nose load 8.205 percent; 26 tests, 516 total pass

title: Add control surfaces, flaps, and slats
description: Deflection of a control surface changes the zero lift angle of its strips. Flaps change camber and drag. The automatic leading edge slats open when the local angle of attack of an outer strip passes a threshold, and they raise the stall angle of that strip by about 6 degrees.
close_reason: Flap CLmax bug fixed in surface.ts, systems.ts with flaps, gear, auto slats, brakes, fuel; 30 tests pass

title: Define the Me-262 geometry and mass
description: Place all 30 elements: 8 strips per wing with cosine spacing, 4 tail strips, 2 fin strips, 1 fuselage body, and 2 nacelle bodies. Set mass, center of gravity, and the inertia tensor. No source publishes the inertia tensor, so estimate it with a lumped mass model and record the method in the document.

title: Model the Jumo 004 B engine
description: Rotor with inertia. States OFF, STARTER, LIGHT_OFF, IDLE, RUNNING, STALL, FLAMEOUT, and FIRE. Idle to full power takes 8 to 10 seconds. A fast throttle increase below 6000 rpm causes a compressor surge. A 2D table gives thrust against Mach number and altitude. Track gas temperature and fuel flow.
close_reason: Jumo 004 B with real gas path and torque balance; 26 tests pass, spool 8.46 s, SFC emergent at 1.427

title: Write the stall model
description: Use a Kirchhoff separation point. The point moves forward as the angle of attack grows. Add a first order lag on the separation point so the model shows dynamic stall. Move the center of pressure back as the flow separates.
close_reason: Full-circle airfoil tables, Kirchhoff stall with LB lag, Mach corrections; 93 tests, 241 total pass

title: Write the aero surface element
description: One element takes its position, area, chord, and orientation. It computes the local air velocity from the body velocity, the angular velocity, and the wind. It returns force and moment in body axes, and it also returns the local angle of attack for the debug view.
close_reason: Strip theory core: lift slope within 0.03 percent of finite span theory, emergent roll damping, asymmetric stall and slat authority; 98 tests, 389 total pass

title: Start the WebGPU renderer

close_reason: WebGPU renderer with WebGL2 fallback, frames.ts, free camera, gamepad reader, input debug panel; 120 tests pass, typecheck clean

title: Build the airfoil coefficient tables
description: Generate CL, CD, and CM against angle of attack from -180 to +180 degrees for NACA 00011 and NACA 00009. Join the attached region, the separation region, and the flat plate region with a smooth blend. Test that the curves stay continuous.
close_reason: Full-circle airfoil tables, Kirchhoff stall with LB lag, Mach corrections; 93 tests, 241 total pass

title: Write the rigid body and the RK4 integrator
description: Hold position, velocity, attitude quaternion, and angular velocity. Apply force and moment in body axes. Integrate with RK4. Renormalize the quaternion each step. Test with known cases: free fall, constant torque, and gyroscopic precession.
close_reason: ISA atmosphere and 6-DOF rigid body with RK4; 34 tests, 120 total pass

title: Write the ISA atmosphere model

title: Build the fixed step loop

title: Write the units module and the interpolation tables

title: The propagation stage, with the delay, the doppler and the air absorption
description: src/audio/sound.ts. One delay line per source at the distance over the speed of sound. A ramp of that delay gives the doppler shift for nothing, because a variable delay line IS the doppler. The distance also takes the high frequencies off, which is what makes a far jet a rumble.

It turns the rotor speed, the thrust, the dynamic pressure, the distance and the Mach number into frequencies, gains and filter cutoffs. title: Open the hood shell of the exterior model at the sill
description:
canopyRing() of src/render/models/me262.ts closes every canopy section with a flat line of points along the sill. loft() then carries that line into a glass FLOOR at y = 0.56, and canopyHoop() wraps the same closed section, so each hood frame carries a solid bar across the cockpit at the sill line, 16 mm thick and 44 mm deep.

A hood is open at the bottom. The bar at station 3.76 belongs to the SLIDING hood, so on a real aircraft that bar would sweep through the chest of the pilot when the hood opens. The bar is a modelling artifact, not framing.

Measured from the eye of the pilot at body (1.61, 0, -0.82):
  windscreen-hoop-1 at station 3.72 fills 29.9 to 31.4 deg below the horizon.
  canopy-hoop-0 at station 3.76 fills 32.3 to 36.9 deg below the horizon.
Together they hide the whole second row of dials. Screenshot: scratchpad/b36v/d8-fault-hoops-as-built.png.

The same closed section puts a glass floor and two flat glass caps at station 3.74 in the line of sight. The forward view therefore crosses four sheets of 30 percent glass and goes milky. That is the approach view.

THE CHANGE
1. Give canopyRing() a flag that leaves out the sill line, so the ring is the crown arc alone (13 points).
2. Build the windscreen loft, the hood loft and canopyHoop() from crown only rings, with closedProfile false.
3. Drop capEnd from the windscreen loft and capStart from the hood loft. Those two flat discs both sit at station 3.74 and both stand in the forward view. Keep capStart on the windscreen: with a crown only ring the cap fan closes over the sill chord, which is the flat front panel of the windscreen.
4. Then delete EXTERIOR_HIDDEN_IN_COCKPIT and buildHoodOccluder() from src/render/models/cockpit.ts. Both work around this fault and nothing else.

Proven at run time on the WebGPU backend: an index over the crown triangles alone gives the correct arch and a clear forward view. Screenshots: scratchpad/b36v/d6-open-hood-shell.png and d7-open-hood-with-fixed-hoops.png against d0-base.png.
close_reason: Canopy rings are crown only. Bounding box identical, triangles 13124 to 12670 with every part matching the loft formula. Hoops now sit above the horizon. Approach contrast: luminance deviation 30.4 to 41.9, black point 42 to 3. Exterior unchanged.

title: Wire the recoil wrench into the aircraft
description:
The armament computes recoil and nothing applies it. src/aircraft/aircraft.ts was owned by the tuning agent, so the weapons agent designed the join to plug in with no second edit. RecoilTarget holds externalWrench as optional, so the code compiles today and does nothing.

Four lines are needed in aircraft.ts:
1. Add externalWrench of type Wrench to the Aircraft interface.
2. In createAircraft, const externalWrench = createWrench().
3. Add externalWrench to the returned api object.
4. In source(), after the thrust block, call addWrench(out, externalWrench).

Firing all four guns then decelerates the aircraft by 0.126 g and pitches the nose up. Do this after bead b33 lands, because b33 owns aircraft.ts.
close_reason: Load limits from the German H 5 stress group with the 1.8 factor, limit and ultimate with different consequences, overspeed aileron jam, engine fire drill, fuel unporting, tire burst warning. Recoil hook added. 722 tests, 31/31 flight rows held.

title: Check whether 18.5 degrees is leading edge sweep, not quarter chord
description:
CONVENTIONS section 8 calls 18.5 degrees the sweep at the quarter chord. The b64 agent reports that sources give 18.5 degrees as the LEADING EDGE sweep, and that the quarter chord sweep is near 16 degrees.

The wing tapers from 2.40 m at the root to 1.07 m at the tip over a 6.255 m semi span, so the two angles differ by about 3 degrees. That is not a rounding difference.

It matters twice. First, sweep relief in compressibility.ts uses the quarter chord angle. Second, and larger, the center of gravity was derived as 25 percent of the mean aerodynamic chord using 18.5 degrees. At the 2.728 m mean aerodynamic chord station the quarter chord line sits 0.913 m aft at 18.5 degrees and 0.782 m aft at 16 degrees. The center of gravity would move about 0.13 m FORWARD, which changes the static margin.

This is the third suspect number found in that table. Check it against a three view and correct the table, the geometry and the render model together.
close_reason: Sweep corrected: 18.5 deg is leading edge, quarter chord is 15.72 deg. AC shift split measured at 94.3 percent from the section, which is wrong but the total is right. Inboard slat panel is real but the strip grid cannot carry it. 31/31 still pass.

title: Re-specify the three Mach test rows that cannot be met
description:
The b58 agent fixed the Mach tuck. Three rows in test/flight/mach.test.ts still read FAIL, and it argued that two of them are mis-specified rather than unmet. Judge each and rewrite the target, or keep it and say why.

1. Largest nose down Cm change targets -0.01 plus or minus 0.005. That is a DETECTION THRESHOLD, not a physical target. The model now gives -0.061. Any model with a real tuck must overshoot a threshold. This row should be a floor, not a band.

2. Mach limit, elevator authority asks for full nose up elevator to fail to make a nose up moment at the 1 g angle of attack. At 8000 m that angle carries a lift coefficient of 0.16. With a zero lift moment of +0.045 the airframe would need a static margin near 0.7 MAC. Real transonic neutral point travel is 0.15 to 0.25 MAC. Check this arithmetic. If it holds, the row asks for something no aerodynamic center shift can give.

3. The dive needs 0.1 more elevator row wants a change of +0.1 where another row caps the same quantity at +0.2. The model gives +0.026. The dive sits at a lift coefficient of 0.10, where the tuck moment scales with lift and is intrinsically small.

Research what the real Me-262 Mach limit behavior was before you rewrite anything. The aircraft was recoverable if the pilot reduced thrust and used the trim wheel. It was not an unrecoverable trap. Write tests that capture the real behavior.
close_reason: One brake fade model in gear.ts, re-derived from real materials; the old one never faded at all. All 6 Mach rows now pass, with two circular or unreachable targets replaced by derived ones.

title: The flap adds no profile drag
description:
Same class of fault as the gear drag in b59. surface.ts reads cd = coefficients.cd + mach.cdAdd + SLAT_OPEN_DRAG times slatOpening. The slat has a profile drag increment. The flap has none, and SurfaceDef carries no flap drag field at all. It holds only flapEffectiveness, flapClMaxDelta and flapAlphaDelta, which are all lift terms.

The flap only shifts alphaTable, which can move cd DOWN. Lowering the flaps therefore costs little or no drag, which is wrong. A landing flap at 50 degrees is a large drag device, and the approach and the landing roll both depend on it.

Add a flap profile drag field to SurfaceDef and apply it the way the slat drag is applied.
close_reason: Flap profile drag from the Hoerner sin squared law, K 0.85 for a slotted flap. Landing L/D 10.77 to 9.19, now below clean at the same speed. 621 tests pass.

title: assembly.evaluate is not a function of its argument
description:
The induced angle pass in assembly.evaluate reads the separation state that the PREVIOUS call left behind. The same input state therefore gives different answers, and near the stall they differ by a factor of four.

The b31 agent had to iterate evaluate to its own fixed point to get a repeatable trim. That is a workaround. The underlying call is impure and every caller is exposed to it.

Also found: the downwash lag never reaches a steady state at finite dt.

Make evaluate a pure function of its arguments, or make the state dependence explicit and documented so a caller can reset it.
close_reason: Mach tuck now appears at 0.825. Root cause was unbounded Prandtl-Glauert plus the tailplane using the wing wave drag table. assembly.evaluate is now pure, spread 0 over repeats. 617 tests pass.

title: Two brake torque constants disagree
description:
gear.ts sets MAX_BRAKE_TORQUE to 12000 N m. systems.ts sets BRAKE_TORQUE_MAX to 4500 N m. gear.ts wins, so the brakes are 2.7 times too strong and the landing roll measures 289 m against an estimate near 800 m.

Pick one value with a stated basis, hold it in one place, and delete the other. CONVENTIONS section 2 says one file holds every tuned number.
close_reason: Gear drag applied at the drag weighted leg position in aircraft.ts and trim.ts; takeoff run 785 to 808 m, now passing. Brake torque unified at 10000 N m in gear.ts. 610 tests pass.

title: The wing does not drop at the stall
description:
At the clean stall the nose drops 14 degrees and the aircraft recovers hands off, with roll at or below 0.3 degrees. With landing flap the nose barely drops, 0.6 degrees, and roll is 0.1 degrees. A wing only drops after a departure with several degrees of sideslip.

The approved plan requires the roll off at the stall to be emergent. The assembly tests do show asymmetric stall in a sideslip, so the mechanism works. The washout and the slats may protect the tip too well, so the whole wing stalls together. Check the washout of 1.5 degrees and the slat span against the real aircraft. Also check that clean CLmax 1.440 against landing 1.622 gives enough margin, since 13 percent is less than the 17 percent the reference expects.
close_reason: NOT A BUG. The aircraft genuinely stalls straight ahead. The wing breaks cleanly at the slat boundary, roll is exactly zero at zero sideslip as symmetry requires, and it grows with sideslip. Assembly CLmax margin is 17.0 percent, matching the reference.

title: Stop the GTAO pass banding the ground at grazing angles
description:
The horizontal bands across the ground come from the GTAO pass in src/render/postfx.ts, not from the ground shader. Proof: a render of the occlusion factor alone reproduces the band pattern, and the same chain with the occlusion multiply removed has no bands.

Cause: the ambient occlusion radius is 0.6 m, which falls below one pixel at distance, and the occlusion target runs at half resolution. On a flat plane at a grazing angle the pass then reports false occlusion in rows.

Measured: aoScale 1 cuts the row to row standard deviation from 34 to 6.8. aoRadius 6 cuts it to 0.55.

Fix in postfx.ts with a distance fade on the occlusion, or hold a minimum screen space radius. A pilot views the ground at a grazing angle on every approach, so this matters more than it would in most scenes. It also makes the WebGL2 picture about one third darker than the WebGPU picture.
close_reason: Distance fade in AO texels; banding std 33.72 to 0.000, backend brightness gap 9.5 to 0.12 percent, contact occlusion survives. Found getViewPosition returns zero on WebGL2.

title: Directional stability is marginal: Cn beta is near zero
description:
The b18 agent measured the yaw stiffness of the complete aircraft. The fin gives +0.077 per radian. The fuselage and the nacelles take -0.075 per radian back. The net is +0.0008 per radian bare, and +0.0039 per radian with the favorable sidewash.

A real fighter has a yaw stiffness near +0.05 to +0.15 per radian. A value of +0.004 is almost neutral. The aircraft would have very weak weathercock stability, poor dutch roll damping, and it would not track straight after an engine failure. The Me-262 did not behave that way.

Two suspects, both marked low confidence by the b17 agent:
1. The vertical tail volume is 0.0319. A 1944 fighter usually sits between 0.04 and 0.06. The fin may be too small or too close to the center of gravity.
2. The fin effective aspect ratio is an estimate. It sets the fin lift curve slope directly.

A third possibility is that the body yaw Munk moment is too strong.

Bead b33 must test this. An engine-out yaw test is the clearest check, because the Me-262 had to stay controllable on one engine.
close_reason: Root cause was a wrong height in the reference table. Fin span 1.67 to 2.00 m. Yaw stiffness +0.0043 to +0.0393. Full rudder now holds one dead engine at 305 km/h against the 300 km/h pilot note.

title: Add the engine start sequence
description: The Riedel starter spins the rotor, then fuel and ignition follow. A rushed start gives a hot start and damage. Add the air relight, which needs speed inside a window and the throttle at idle.
close_reason: Handbook start sequence step by step, crank to idle 80 s to 39 s after fixing a starter torque curve that gave zero surplus power at the light off speed. Hot relight above 6000 rpm. Pooled fuel now purges. 45 engine tests, 31/31 flight.

title: Build the instruments
description: Airspeed in km/h, altimeter in m, artificial horizon, variometer, turn and slip, compass, fuel, and rotor speed and gas temperature for each engine. Draw each face once on a canvas and rotate a needle mesh every frame.
close_reason: Fifteen live instruments with German markings and researched dial laws, masked drum horizon with gyro erection error, per instrument needle lag. 83 tests added, 805 total pass.

title: Carry the corrected sweep into the render model and the mass model
description:
Bead b65 corrected the quarter chord sweep from 18.5 to 15.72 degrees in geometry.ts and compressibility.ts. Three files still hold the old angle. The b65 agent did not own them.

1. src/render/models/me262.ts near line 299: WING_SWEEP becomes 15.72 degrees. Near line 302: WING_ROOT_QUARTER_Z becomes 4.992 minus CG_OFFSET_FROM_NOSE. The header comment near lines 40 to 45 restates the derivation.
2. src/aircraft/me262/mass.ts near line 131: TAN_SWEEP uses 15.72 degrees. Near line 137: WING_ROOT_QUARTER_STATION becomes 4.992. The effect on the computed center of gravity is 2.4 mm, which is negligible, but the wing lumps must sit on the same line as the aerodynamic strips.
3. src/physics/aero/downwash.ts near line 195: a comment cites 18.5 degrees in the DATCOM sidewash sum. Redoing it at 15.72 gives 0.222 against 0.224 and leaves SIDEWASH_SLOPE unchanged. Comment only.

close_reason: Tuck split corrected: wing section shift 97.2 to 64.9 percent, everything else 0.4 to 31.8 percent. Downwash slope now falls 0.562 to 0.249 and tail efficiency 0.920 to 0.817. Total travel and onset unchanged. Sweep carried into the render and mass models, bounding box unchanged. 846 tests, 31/31.

title: Move the Mach tuck from the section shift to the tail and the downwash
description:
Measured by the b66 agent between Mach 0.78 and 0.86 at 8000 m. The neutral point moves 0.242 MAC, which is right and inside the published band. The parts are wrong.

Section aerodynamic center shift on the wing strips gives 94.3 percent of it. The tailplane shift gives 2.7 percent. Everything else gives 3.0 percent.

The three effects that should carry a tuck carry none. The downwash slope RISES from 0.550 to 0.555, which is the wrong way. The tail efficiency holds at exactly 0.920. The tailplane lift curve slope falls only 1.2 percent.

NACA TN 3501, Nelson and McDevitt 1955, measures section travel of 0.07 chord by Mach 0.85, reaching 0.39 chord only above Mach 0.95. AC_SHIFT_X runs the section from 0.25 to 0.50, which is far past the real value.

The fix needs a Mach dependent downwash slope and a falling tail dynamic pressure in downwash.ts, then a refit of AC_SHIFT_X. Do not change the total. It is correct and the tuck onset measures 0.825 against 0.83.
close_reason: Tuck split corrected: wing section shift 97.2 to 64.9 percent, everything else 0.4 to 31.8 percent. Downwash slope now falls 0.562 to 0.249 and tail efficiency 0.920 to 0.817. Total travel and onset unchanged. Sweep carried into the render and mass models, bounding box unchanged. 846 tests, 31/31.

title: Full stick above 600 km/h still passes the limit load, whatever the input scaling
description:
Bead b56 item 4 added controlAuthority to src/input/bindings.ts. It scales the three flight commands by 10 kPa over the dynamic pressure, which is the stick force law of an unboosted control, and it removes the step that a key press used to make: a snatch to full stick at 3000 m and Mach 0.75 reaches 8.87 g after 0.25 s instead of 12.33 g.

It does not cap a pilot who HOLDS the stick. A sweep of a constant pitch command against the peak load factor of a three second pull at 3000 m gives:

  400 km/h  q 5612 Pa   full command peaks at 3.09 g
  500 km/h  q 8769 Pa   full command peaks at 4.96 g
  600 km/h  q 12627 Pa  0.30 of the command peaks at 6.85 g
  700 km/h  q 17186 Pa  0.05 of the command peaks at 6.03 g
  800 km/h and above    no command at all stays under 7 g

Five percent of the elevator, which is 1.3 degrees, gives 6 g at 700 km/h. No bound on the deflection can both leave the pilot able to maneuver at 500 km/h and hold the aircraft inside the envelope at 800 km/h.

Decide whether that is right. The classic result says the elevator angle per g is nearly independent of speed for a rigid stable aircraft, and this model gives an angle per g that falls much faster than that. Either the pitch damping Cmq is too small, or the elevator power Cmde is too large, or the transient overshoot of the short period is not being damped. Read src/aircraft/me262/geometry.ts and src/physics/aero/surface.ts against a published Me 262 short period.

This is not a display fault. src/ui/hud.ts already warns at the live limit and src/main.ts already shows the failure.

title: The fog turns everything above 5 km milk white
description:
The FogExp2 fit is tuned for a view from the ground: 3 percent at 3 km and 98 percent at 30 km. Seen from 6300 m looking down, it washes the whole picture out.

The b43 agent verified this against a control frame with the cloud mesh hidden, so it is not the clouds. It is pre-existing.

This matters because the aircraft spends most of its time between 6000 m and 11450 m. Fog that is right for a taxi view is wrong for the cruise.

The fix is height aware fog. Real haze sits in the boundary layer and thins fast with altitude, so the density should fall with height rather than stay constant. Keep the ground level appearance, which is correct now, and make the air above about 3 km clear.
close_reason: Height aware fog from the exact optical depth of an exponential aerosol profile; ground view pixel identical, high altitude now clear. Performance: the processor was the limit, not the card. Hiding empty LOD levels cut 107 null draws per frame, scatter 2.4 ms to 0.7 ms.

title: A hot engine should relight without closing the throttle
description:
engine.ts refuses a relight above 5 percent throttle. That rule is right for a cold windmill start. It is wrong for an engine that flamed out a second ago with the rotor still spinning near idle speed.

Found by bead b39: a negative g fuel interruption in a dive killed both engines for the whole dive, because the throttle was open and neither could relight while the rotor was still turning fast.

Allow a hot relight while the rotor is above a stated speed, and keep the closed throttle rule for a cold air start.
close_reason: Handbook start sequence step by step, crank to idle 80 s to 39 s after fixing a starter torque curve that gave zero surplus power at the light off speed. Hot relight above 6000 rpm. Pooled fuel now purges. 45 engine tests, 31/31 flight.

title: Wire the failure banner and the mass aware g limit

1. src/main.ts near line 419: create a banner, subscribe to aircraft.events failure, show the message, and hide it after a few seconds. A failure the pilot cannot read is a bug.
2. src/ui/hud.ts: loadFactorLevel hard codes plus 7 and minus 3. It must read aircraft.structure.state.limits, so the G LIMIT warning follows mass and damage. The limit falls to 6.28 g at maximum takeoff mass and falls again by 30 percent once the wing is bent.

Both files were owned by other agents when b39 finished.
close_reason: HUD clear of the debug panel, failure banner wired, g limit reads live limits, interior bow removed, Z and C for differential braking, control authority scaled in the input layer where it cannot touch the measurements. 839 tests, 31/31.

title: The tire friction has no speed term and a locked wheel grips too well
description:
LONG_SHAPE is 1.45, so the magic formula gives a locked wheel 82 percent of the peak coefficient at a slip of -1. With LONG_PEAK_MU at 0.8 a skidding tire therefore holds 0.656 at any speed. Measured aircraft tires on dry concrete hold about half of the peak at 95 kt, and the value falls with ground speed on the peak side as well.

Bead b33 measured the effect: with the old 10000 N m brake the aircraft locked both wheels from the first touch of the pedal and stopped in 281 m at a mean of 0.52 g, which is harder than a modern jet with anti-skid. Bead b33 fixed the ROLL through MAX_BRAKE_TORQUE, which is the constant the pilot notes measure, so the wheel now turns and the tire curve no longer sets the answer. The tire is still wrong.

Work: add a speed term to the longitudinal peak, or deepen the falling side of the curve. test/unit/gear.test.ts asserts that a locked tire keeps 60 to 90 percent of the peak, and that assertion moves with the shape.

title: A fuselage pays the wave drag of an 11 percent wing
description:
evaluateBody of src/physics/aero/body.ts calls machCorrection with a sweep of zero and no thickness, so every body reads the wave drag table of the REFERENCE SECTION, which is the 11 percent wing root. The table anchors carry the cosine of the reference sweep, so a body starts its drag rise at free stream Mach 0.740 and pays the full section value on its frontal area.

A slender fuselage of fineness 8 does not do that. Its drag rise starts far higher, near Mach 0.9, and it is smaller when it comes. Bead b33 measured the cost: at Mach 0.788 the fuselage and the two nacelles added 0.0023 to CD, which was the WHOLE drag rise the aircraft felt at 6000 m, while the wing added 0.0002.

No row depends on it now, because the 6000 m level speed settles at Mach 0.740 after the drag correction of bead b33. It will matter again to any bead that touches the level speed at height or the dive.

Work: give a body its own drag rise, from the fineness ratio, or pass the body a thickness and a sweep that mean something.

title: The maximum speed gains too little with altitude
description:
The published pair is 827 km/h at sea level and 870 km/h at 6000 m, a gain of 43 km/h. After bead b33 the model gives 827.2 and 842.6, a gain of 15 km/h. Both rows pass their 5 percent bands, so the fault is the TREND and not either point.

The cause is the thrust lapse. THRUST_ALTITUDE_EXPONENT is 1.0, and a jet with a lapse exponent of 1 holds the same maximum speed at every height, because V^2 goes as thrust over density. The published pair asks for an exponent near 0.84 on its own. The model also multiplies the thrust by thrustSpeedFraction of the CORRECTED rotor speed, which costs 12 percent at sea level at Mach 0.68 and nothing at 6000 m, because the clamp holds it at 1. That term already leans the other way and gives the 15 km/h.

Work: measure the thrust of the engine model against Mach and height, compare it against a momentum estimate at a fixed physical rotor speed, and judge THRUST_MACH_FACTOR and THRUST_ALTITUDE_EXPONENT together. The ceiling row is the constraint: it passes now at 11176 m and it falls with any steeper lapse.

title: Check how the aerodynamic center shift splits between section and downwash
description:
AC_SHIFT_X moves the SECTION aerodynamic center from 0.25 to 0.50 chord. The b64 agent cites NACA TN 3501, which puts section aerodynamic center travel at only about 7 percent of chord by Mach 0.85.

The whole aircraft answer is right. The neutral point moves 0.17 MAC aft between Mach 0.78 and 0.86, inside the published 0.15 to 0.25 band, and the tuck onset measures 0.825 against 0.83. So the total is correct.

The concern is the SPLIT. If the real section shift is small, then most of the whole aircraft travel should come from the tail losing effectiveness and from the downwash, not from the section. A model that gets the right total from the wrong parts will drift when anything nearby changes.

Read TN 3501 and check the split. Do not change the total unless the evidence says the total is wrong.
close_reason: Sweep corrected: 18.5 deg is leading edge, quarter chord is 15.72 deg. AC shift split measured at 94.3 percent from the section, which is wrong but the total is right. Inboard slat panel is real but the strip grid cannot carry it. 31/31 still pass.

title: Two brake fade models both apply

This is pre-existing and was outside the scope of b59 and b60. Pick one owner. The physics layer is the natural place, because src/physics sits below src/aircraft and cannot import upward, which is the same reasoning that put the brake torque constant in gear.ts.
close_reason: One brake fade model in gear.ts, re-derived from real materials; the old one never faded at all. All 6 Mach rows now pass, with two circular or unreachable targets replaced by derived ones.

title: Add the inboard slat panel between the fuselage and the nacelle
description:
The A-1a carried three separate slat panels per wing. The innermost sat between the fuselage and the nacelle. The leading edge was therefore slatted over almost the full span, broken only at the nacelle.

The model carries slats only from y 3.0 to 6.02 m, which is the outer 48 percent. The b49 agent verified this against sources and recorded it in the SLAT_SPAN comment.

Adding the inboard panel makes the stall MORE docile and lowers the stall speed. That would push the landing stall below the 180 km/h handbook floor, so this bead must re-calibrate at the same time. Do not add the panel alone.
close_reason: Sweep corrected: 18.5 deg is leading edge, quarter chord is 15.72 deg. AC shift split measured at 94.3 percent from the section, which is wrong but the total is right. Inboard slat panel is real but the strip grid cannot carry it. 31/31 still pass.

title: Correct seven stale comments and one number mismatch
description:
Writing the documents found seven places where a code comment no longer matches the code. None changes behavior. All mislead a reader.

1. surface.ts line 142 says the swept strip couple factor is 0.90 on this wing. That is the cosine squared of 18.5 degrees. At the corrected 15.72 degrees it is 0.927.
2. downwash.ts line 597 cites a fin of aspect ratio 1.5. geometry.ts derives an effective 1.97 from a geometric 1.08.
3. engine.ts line 572 says the motoring drag holds 800 rpm against the starter. The constant power balance in the same file gives 1191 rpm. The 800 rpm figure belongs to the superseded linear starter curve.
4. geometry.ts line 228 cites a section lift curve slope of 6.5 per radian for the Oswald fit. airfoil.ts gives 6.82 inviscid and cites about 6.13 measured.
5. Bead 7el records a fuselage drag rise starting at Mach 0.740. At the corrected sweep it is 0.751.
6. FUEL_FLOW_AT_MAX_POWER in engine.ts line 127 is exported and never imported. It documents a model output, not an input. Say so or stop exporting it.

ONE REAL NUMBER MISMATCH, not a comment:
7. mass.ts lines 114 to 116 derive the ammunition mass as 0.48 kg times 360 rounds plus ten percent, which is 190 kg. AMMUNITION_MASS is 176 kg. Find which is right. The mass model and the weapons model must agree on how much ammunition the aircraft carries.

title: Give a strip a slat coverage fraction, then add the inboard slat panel
description:
The A-1a carried three unconnected slat sections on each wing, fastened by two hinges each, over the full span. Source: Stapfer, Messerschmitt Me 262, pages 31 and 36. The model carries only the outer panels.

The b57 agent measured the effect. Outer panels only gives a landing stall of 182.0 km/h. Moving the outer panel in to the nacelle gives 173.1. Adding the inboard panel as well gives 160.4, which is 20 km/h below the handbook floor of 180.

Two things block it. SurfaceDef has no slat coverage fraction, so a strip takes the whole 6 degree stall delta or none, and the inboard panel runs 0.55 to 1.60 m while the first cosine strip runs 0.00 to 1.22 m. The grid cannot represent the panel honestly.

Note that the sources disagree with each other. Stapfer gives 160 to 170 km/h for the slatted aircraft, which is where the model already lands with all three panels. The pilot handbook gives 180 to 202. Resolve which configuration each number describes before calibrating.

title: Close the pilot facing gaps found on the first flight
description: 1. The gear legs are rigid rods, so a landing shows no oleo stroke. The physics computes 0.154 m of static compression and the model must show it. 2. Differential braking has no keyboard binding. Only the gamepad triggers separate left from right. 3. A hot start is unrecoverable and nothing tells the pilot why the relight fails. 4. Full elevator at Mach 0.75 gives more than 3 g at once, because there is no control authority scaling with dynamic pressure.
notes:
Item 1 is DONE. The gear legs telescope. Each leg has a fixed gas cylinder and a sliding piston on a GearSlider node that carries the piston, the torque link and the wheel pivot, so the axle stays on the piston. The slide is scaled by 1 over up.y, because the model legs rake 6.9 degrees at the nose and 14.5 degrees at the mains while the physics strut acts on body z. main.ts now calls setGearCompression each frame.

The fin correction from b49 also landed in the render model. The bounding box now measures 12.510 by 3.830 by 10.600 m. Triangles 12884 to 13124.

Item 2 is DONE. Z brakes the left wheel and C brakes the right wheel. The two keys sit one column under Q and E, which are the rudder keys, so the brake of a side is under the same finger as the rudder of that side. B still brakes both. The keys carry no taxi gate, unlike the gamepad triggers, because a key that drives nothing else cannot fight the rudder. The pilot can therefore hold the aircraft straight through the whole landing roll.

Item 3 is DONE for the display half. The engine model writes Engine.message and Engine.startPhase. hud.ts prints the message across the top of the systems bar, over the ENG 1 and ENG 2 cells, and engineMessageText prints each distinct line one time with the engines that raised it.

Item 4 is DONE, with a measured bound on what it achieves. controlAuthority of src/input/bindings.ts scales the roll, pitch and yaw commands by FULL_AUTHORITY_PRESSURE over the dynamic pressure, floored at 0.15. The law is the stick force of an unboosted control: the hinge moment follows the dynamic pressure and the pilot has a fixed maximum pull, so the deflection falls as one over q. The reference is 10 kPa, which is 456 km/h EAS, so the takeoff, the approach and a stall recovery keep every degree. The scaling lives in the INPUT layer, so the trim solver and the flight test harness are untouched.

Measured, a snatch to full stick at 3000 m and Mach 0.75 held for three seconds: 12.33 g after 0.25 s before the change and 8.87 g after it, peak 13.74 g before and 13.02 g after. Above about 600 km/h the elevator of this airframe reaches the stall angle at a few degrees of deflection, so no bound on the deflection alone holds the aircraft inside the envelope.
